newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai news ignored by Singapore rubber market.
newsitem.headline: Thai news ignored by Singapore rubber market.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market ignored news the Thai government clinched a deal for China to buy 382,000 tonnes of rubber while keeping an eye on the strike by 13,000 workers of Goodyear, dealers said on Tuesday.
Trading in the market was mostly quiet by midday with one spot deal for RSS1 grade rubber done, they said.
"It's a fig leaf. The Thais probably asked the Chinese to give them a number, and the Chinese said fine but they did not give a timeframe for buying the rubber," one trader said.
One dealer said the critical details such as price and shipment periods will still be negotiated next month.

"We won't see a reaction in the trade until then," he said. The only business seen done was for RSS1 rubber. "We managed to clinch a deal for several hundred tonnes of RSS1 rubber by a local outfit doing some shortcovering. The rest of the market though was quiet," a dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 106.00-108.00 U.S. cents a kg from 108.50 cents.

June RSS1 was seen at 153.50-155.50 Singapore cents (US$1.06-$1.08) a kg from 156.25 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 149.00-151.00 Singapore cents (US$1.03-$1.05) a kg from 150.00 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
